text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States ambassador in Nicosia visits Brussels for important talks with the European Union on Cyprus.
- The prices commission is to review the price of staple food products.
- Only two licences for the operation of casinos will be issued, says the government.
- Cypriot widow of silver bullet victim is questioned by British detectives.
- The government plans three-year jail term for bosses who hire illegal workers.
- We are not satisfied with the government and want a new president, says communist party chief Demetris Christofias.
- Greece's deputy foreign minister starts contacts in Cyprus for a "fruitful cooperation" with Greece on the Cyprus issue before initiatives to settle the problem start.
- Cyprus has cards up its sleeve in the course towards European Union accession in the event of objections from community members who want the Cyprus problem solved first.
- The House of Representatives is set to intervene on government plans to deregulate interest rates.
- Father of Greek Cypriot youth shot dead offers a 10,000 pound reward for the arrest of a Turk suspected of his killing.
- University senate's decision to remove the Greek flag from building sparks angry reaction from students.
- Two foreign firms take the Cyprus electricity authority to court demanding their tenders be accepted for supply of turbines in power plant.
